text: The human takes AI cities on the turn it declares, after staging its units next to them at peace (study/staging.md: games 1-5). The AI cannot answer by construction: a city's danger counts only units of a team already at war and only on the city's own area, so a staged army or one aboard ships counts nothing, and the defenders a city wants do not rise. A city that sizes its defence by the exact assault forecast of the foreign units able to reach it this turn, at peace or at war and aboard ships, loses fewer cities to that strike.

change: Change S on (define AI_STAGED_FORECAST, per mille, off at 0): in CvCityAI::AI_neededDefenders, the land units able to attack that could reach the city this turn, of teams that are not the owner's, its vassal or its master, counted by their moves (units aboard a ship by the ship's moves), are given to AI_assaultForecast against the city's defenders; while the forecast is at least the threshold (AI_STAGED_FORECAST plus ten times the leader's attack-odds change), the city wants one defender more than it has, and while it would be at least the threshold with one defender fewer, it keeps the ones it has. An AI at peace counts another AI's units only if its attitude allows war (the test of the paranoia code); a human's always. Built on the war-log DLL with the four war-AI fixes (builds/staging); only games written by builds made under P3 count, so games for P2 and for P3 never mix.

reason: Before any evidence or build: measured on the saves of games 3 to 5 (HARNESS_DEFENCE_DIAG), raising the defenders a city wants changes them in 6 of 511 AI cities, since city production reads that count only once the city is in danger and about half of all AI cities are already below it. The change is replaced by P4, which also feeds the city's danger flag.

change: Change S2 on (define AI_STAGED_FORECAST, per mille, off at 0). The staged forecast: the land units able to attack that could reach the city this turn, of teams that are not the owner's, its vassal or its master, counted by their moves (units aboard a ship by the ship's moves), given to AI_assaultForecast against the city's land defenders; an AI at peace counts another AI's units only if its attitude allows war (the test of the paranoia code), a human's always. The threshold is AI_STAGED_FORECAST plus ten times the leader's attack-odds change. While the forecast reaches the threshold, the city is in danger (CvCityAI::AI_isDanger, which city production and the city governor read) and wants one defender more than it has (AI_neededDefenders); while it would reach it with one defender fewer, it keeps the ones it has. Danger as unit moves and workers read it (CvPlayerAI::AI_getPlotDanger) is unchanged. Built on the war-log DLL with the four war-AI fixes (builds/staging); only games written by builds made under P4 count, so games for P2 and for P4 never mix.

text: No AI ever moves against the human, even while it leads and while it is at war with one of them (study/doctrine.md, R2: games 1-5). By construction: every war path of CvTeamAI::AI_doWar wants a target weaker than the AI alone and passes a no-war roll against the leader's NoWarAttitudeProbs for its attitude, which the human keeps high with gifts and open borders (R3); the one coalition path (dogpile) counts only the power of teams already at war with the target; and a team with any war plan does not consider a new war. Measured first at the saves (study/d3-design.md, step 1). AIs that weigh a hegemon by their leader's own envy and count the others who would join take more back from the human and let it take less.

text: The game froze when the user founded the first city with the paging build (PythonDbg.log ends after 'City Built Event: London' and the score update; LSystem.log has just laid out the city). Of what paging destroys, only the plot builder is never destroyed by vanilla during a game (CvPlot::uninit alone calls PlotBuilderIFace destroy; feature, route, yield and flag symbols and unit and city entities are destroyed and remade in vanilla play), and plot builders share the executable's L-system with city layouts, the first of which is made at the first city. Keeping plot builders removes the freeze. Contradicted if the game still freezes at the first city with GRAPHICS_PAGING_PLOT_BUILDERS 0, or does not freeze with it 1. The harness has no executable, so only the user's game decides; separately CvGameInterface.getCameraZoom took no argument and failed once (PythonErr.log).

text: The mod's Assets/Python/EntryPoints/CvGameInterface.py, added for the camera in !57 (ccbc1b5, 'the Beyond the Sword file unchanged'), is not the Beyond the Sword file. It defines 49 functions plus the camera's, its gameUtils() returns a plain CvGameUtils.CvGameUtils(), and it never imports CvGameInterfaceFile. Facts: the original BTS SDK in the GitLab repository (beyond-the-sword-sdk-develop-functional.tar.gz) calls 22 CvGameInterface functions that the file lacks (PYGameModule is "CvGameInterface"; among them getUnitCostMod, getBuildingCostMod, getUpgradePriceOverride, getExperienceNeeded, doPillageGold, doCityCaptureGold, getExtraCost, canBuild, cannotFoundCity); the mod ships BUG's CvGameInterfaceFile.py, 'Overrides the use of CvGameUtils with BUG's modular game utils dispatcher', and registers RoMGameUtils through it (Assets/Config/RoMSettings.xml) with RoM's rules for cannotConstruct, cannotDoCivic, getUnitCostMod, getBuildingCostMod, getUpgradePriceOverride, doPillageGold and doCityCaptureGold; PythonCallbackDefines.xml switches the unit cost, building cost, upgrade price, cannot-construct and cannot-do-civic callbacks on, and calculateExperience calls getExperienceNeeded with no switch. Since the mod's file replaces the game's in play, RoM's Python rules have not run since !57. Moving getCameraView to the mod's own CvScreensInterface.py (PYScreensModule, which the DLL already calls) and deleting the mod's CvGameInterface.py restores the game's file and BUG's dispatcher and keeps the camera window. Contradicted if the installed Beyond the Sword Assets/Python/EntryPoints/CvGameInterface.py is the same file (49 functions, no CvGameInterfaceFile import), or if a game on main 4ec8ebc applies RoM's missionary cost (75 % under a state religion civic, RoMGameUtils.getUnitCostMod).

text: The AI's trade values and offers do not follow the game's rules (GitLab main 3bec049). Facts: (1) every offer it makes starts from a uniform random draw (getSorenRandNum(10000)) among the partner's tradeable techs or spare resources: tech purchases, tech swaps, tech sales, help requests and resource swaps (CvPlayerAI::AI_doDiplo); (2) CvTeamAI::AI_techTradeVal prices a tech from CvTeam::getResearchCost, ignoring the receiver's research modifier (TECH_DIFFUSION_ENABLE 1, up to +30% from known teams; known-prerequisite modifiers 15); (3) CvPlayerAI::AI_bonusTradeVal values a resource at a fixed +100 per happiness or health and half a point per percent of building yield modifier (AI_baseBonusVal), scaled by the smaller of the two players' city counts, with no regard to whether its cities are unhappy or unhealthy or to the production and commerce its cities make (Town Essentials: Coffee +20% production, +10% commerce; Forge: Gold +25% commerce); (4) AI_maxGoldTrade lets an AI with non-negative income trade its whole treasury, ignoring AI_goldTarget. In the user's game 4 (turns 264-268) three AIs paid 380-660 gold, 59-98% of their treasuries, for randomly chosen techs (Archery, Fermentation), and AIs paid the human 2,545 gold over turns 254-285 against the human's own income of 4,238. Valuing techs by the receiver's effective cost, resources by their effect in the valuer's own cities, choosing what to ask for and give by value, refusing to sell techs to a higher-ranked team, and keeping the gold target in tech purchases makes the AI pay what a trade is worth to it and stop funding the leader. Contradicted if, in the user's games with the change, AIs still pay most of their treasury for techs outside their research queue, or still give resources they need for ones they do not.

text: The game crashed while the player zoomed in and out fast at turn 108 of a 20-civilization huge Europe game under Proton (GitLab main 3bec049). Facts from GraphicsPaging.log and PythonDbg.log: 105 passes set up 2,282 plots, 21 units and 7 cities again, at most 238 plots, 2 units and 1 city in one pass; the last, after the window grew from 60 x 43 to 60 x 65 plots in 0.3 s, set up 918 plots, 6 units and 2 cities in one update, and each of those plots also rebuilt its tile art (CvPlot::pageGraphics calls updateFeatureSymbol(true), which calls RebuildTileArt) although paging never removes tile art; no later pass is logged, and Python logged about 4 s more without error. No crash address was obtained. The cause is the executable setting up that much graphics at once: setting up at most GRAPHICS_PAGING_MAX_IN (100) plots, units and cities per update, the rest at the next updates, and not rebuilding the tile art on page-in keeps each update's set-up below what the session survived. Contradicted if the game still crashes when zooming in and out fast with this change, or crashes the same way with GRAPHICS_PAGING 0.

text: Resource records can be added to the mod without changing anything else the player sees or the game does (GitLab main 71de0ab). Facts: CIV4BonusInfos.xml holds 72 live records and one commented out (BONUS_WOOL, lines 4113-4154, whose art define and glyph 101 exist and which nothing else references); the Guilds module adds BONUS_CGUILDPAPER, so the game has 73. CvGameTextMgr::assignFontIds gives resource i the character S + 125 + its FontButtonIndex (CvBonusInfo::setChar adds 125) and puts the 26 extra symbols (happy, health, strength ... airport) at the first multiple of 25 that is at least S + N + 2 for N records, unless WOC_GAMEFONT_RESOURCE_FIX (GlobalDefinesAlt.xml, 0 today) is above 0, which then fixes it. Both GameFont sheets hold the happy face 50 cells before resource cell 0, that is at S + 75, which N = 73 gives and N = 74 to 98 would move to S + 100, an empty row. With the BTS first symbol code 8483, 3 yields, 4 commerce types, 16 religions and 27 corporations, S = 8650 and the happy face is character 8725. Cells 106 to 111 of the resource block are empty in both sheets; Biofuel shows Diesel's glyph 77 (shared art define), Synthetic Rubber Vulcanized Rubber's 99 (shared art define), Smart Medicine Chemicals' 85 (same index). The claim: appending records after the last one keeps every existing resource's index, and pinning WOC_GAMEFONT_RESOURCE_FIX to 8725 keeps every extra symbol where the fonts hold it, so four more records (Wool, Timber, Dairy, Leather) with their own glyphs, and own glyphs for the three shared pairs, neither crash nor slow the game and leave every other symbol unchanged. Contradicted if a run fails only with the change, if the median same-seed turn time rises above 5 %, or if in game any happy, health, strength or other extra symbol, or any existing resource icon, shows a different glyph at either font size. Old saves do not load across the change (the resource arrays grow): it needs a new game.

text: P30 (LQ.F11 no slower) was refuted (median run time +9.1 %). A code review (M42) found that the produced-goods term LQ.F10 added to CvCityAI::AI_bestPlotBuild differs from the resource code it was meant to copy: it boosted every improvement giving a good the plot already gave, including the improvement on the plot, which pushed iValue past the gate (iValue > 0) after which yield boosts are added, so the best-build values of every pasture, latifundium, camp and mill plot were inflated in every city every turn; it ignored the good's trade tech. text: A plot's whole change of goods can be applied as one vector (M43): CvPlotGroup walks its plots once and each city applies all counts and updates its corporations once. The end state equals one good at a time, because CvCity::processBonus is additive (every effect is change(value x iChange), values from buildings that a count change does not alter) and CvCity::updateCorporation recomputes everything it sets from the counts. Before registration, deterministic runs (Mediterranean, seed 485959733, 150 turns): the batched and unbatched DLLs give identical telemetry on GitLab f70541a9 XML (run time 0.999); on 02d5f85a XML (no produced goods) the new and the old DLL give identical telemetry (0.997; seed 2086998694: 0.992). Contradicted if a run fails or the median same-seed run time rises above 5 %.

text: CvPlayerAI::AI_baseBonusVal recomputes each good's value once per turn (and after a team's tech) and, in its building loop, called canConstruct for every building class of the civilization even when no term of the building depends on the good; every later step multiplies, divides or zeroes the building's term, so skipping buildings whose term is 0 leaves the value unchanged. More goods (LQ.F10, LQ.F11) mean more recomputations, so this is part of the cost the goods add (M44). Before registration, deterministic runs (Mediterranean, 150 turns, f70541a9 XML): identical telemetry with and without the gate, run time 0.967 (seed 485959733) and 0.973 (seed 2086998694). Contradicted if a run fails or the median same-seed run time rises above 5 %.
